fit: ethanolic dried-stigma extract and major depression
assessment: In 40 adults over six weeks, Hamilton depression favored 30 mg/day dry extract (F=18.89, p<.001). The primary Methods specify extraction with 80% ethanol. Neither culinary ground stigma nor Parkinson disease was studied.

fit: ground stigma in a single non-Parkinson fluoxetine adjunct family
assessment: The 2018 original used 30 mg/day ground Khorasan stigma and reported intergroup BDI p=.056 with 20 per arm analyzed. The 2015 author abstract reports p=.560 with 19 and 11 completers. The official six-week registration and two four-week reports link to one family; no consistent between-arm estimate or Parkinson population.

fit: saffron extract with sedge and honey in neurocognitive disorder
assessment: The two-month GDS difference was inconclusive (p=.224). The simultaneously assigned ingredients prevent attribution to saffron, and no Parkinson subgroup result was reported.

fit: registered saffron and chamomile combination in Parkinson disease
assessment: Latest accessible registry shows unknown status and no posted results. The investigator letter reports no trial outcomes. No culinary ground saffron or separately estimated depression effect is available.

fit: plant diet indexes and fatigue in older women
assessment: Separate fatigue HRs were 0.79 (95% CI 0.77–0.82) for the healthful index and 1.16 (1.12–1.20) for the unhealthful index, highest versus lowest quintile. Coffee and tea form a combined index item. No coffee-specific fatigue or Parkinson comparison was reported.

fit: saffron capsules and total Parkinson motor score
assessment: The randomized Tehran trial analyzed 52 people across arms and reports motor Part III total p=.424. The public results give no separate rigidity comparison and the capsule preparation was not specified.
